messages:
marta: quick sync thread: we need to lock down the policy-engine contract and hysteresis math for continuous-batcher fallbacks. postmortem showed flip-flopping when eviction TTLs spike. want concrete formulas + telemetry.

ashok: agree. we should treat signals as noisy and apply EWMA smoothing before comparing to thresholds. naive thresholds on instantaneous headroom caused thrash.

zia: what smoothing window? model_token_rate varies a lot per tenant. suggestion: adaptive alpha where alpha = clamp(1 - exp(-dt / tau), 0.01, 0.5). tau per-tenant based on recent variance.

kevin: i like adaptive tau. for cooldowns, propose: cooldown = base_cooldown * (1 + sigmoid(oversubscription_ratio - 1) * scale). base_cooldown = 10s, scale = 5. prevents tiny blips from toggling.

marta: can we write these more concretely in the policy spec? also clear separation: policy-engine decides action, signal-aggregator serves smoothed signals, router executes. batcher/allocator expose minimal hooks.

ashok: rough spec snippet: 
```
SignalAggregator {
  subscribe(tenant, signals[]) -> subscription_id
  get_smoothed(signal_name) -> float // EWMA with adaptive tau
}

FallbackPolicy {
  id: string
  triggers: [ { signal: string, operator: ">", threshold: float, smoothing: {tau_s: float | "adaptive"} } ]
  action: "microbatch" | "variant_swap" | "route_dedicated"
  base_cooldown_s: 10
  cooldown_scale: 5
  min_duration_s: 5
}
```

zia: about eviction ownership: allocator should remain the single source of truth for unit accounting. batcher calls allocator.evict_hint(tenant, requested_units) which returns granted_eviction and recommended_force_evict boolean. that keeps complexity out of batcher.

kevin: small counterpoint: batcher needs lightweight heuristics for very small requests to fastpath without full allocator roundtrip. propose batcher exposes fastpath_small_request(size_tokens) and meters consumption locally up to a small soft quota (e.g. 100 units) before hitting allocator.

marta: ok hybrid model: allocator authoritative for long-running decisions; batcher has a bounded soft quota for microfast paths. document limits and failure modes.

ashok: telemetry list: per-tenant: headroom_pct_ewma, kv_warmup_rate_ewma, fallback_active{action}, fallback_cooldown_remaining, soft_quota_utilization, allocator_eviction_calls, fastpath_denied_count. tag with policy_id.

zia: add histograms for fallback_duration_seconds and recovery_time_seconds (time from fallback start to return-to-normal). alerting: recovery_time > 60s for >1% tenants -> page.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: feature-branch deploy scheduled 2799991400; will include SignalAggregator + drain_hint stub + soft_quota flag.

kevin: test plan: 1) unit tests for EWMA with adaptive tau; 2) integration: 30s noisy tenant ramp injecting KV misses at fixed rate; expect fallback action within 3-8s and no more than one toggle in 60s; 3) soak: 10 min mixed-traffic test validating p99 latency and cost delta.

marta: ops: lia (cc'd in DM) will add dashboard panels: per-tenant fallback timeline, policy_id heatmap, allocator_eviction_rate. also need a runbook for manual override -> policy disable endpoint.

ashok: code API sketches for drain_hint and fastpath: 
```
// batcher -> allocator
evict_hint(tenant_id: string, desired_release_units: int, urgency: "low"|"high") -> {granted_units: int, force_evict: bool}

// batcher local fastpath
fastpath_consume(tenant_id, units) -> bool // true if within soft quota
```

marta: governance: every policy change must be versioned and rollout via console with staged targets (alpha/beta/all). default global policy kept conservative.

zia: one more: simulate policy collisions: two policies for same tenant (global + tenant-specific) -> combine by priority: tenant policy > team policy > global; document merge semantics.

kevin: owners: ashok -> implement SignalAggregator + EWMA (2w); zia -> allocator evict_hint + runtime soft_quota (2w); marta -> policy CR and rollout plan (1w); lia -> dashboards + alerts (1w).

sre-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2027 to track canary fallback noise; alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.

marta: thanks. sync tomorrow 11am PT. please dump any additional math or test scripts in the RFC doc. :memo:
